candidates_reviewed.name: Agent privacy becomes a runtime governance problem
candidates_reviewed.mechanism: Runtime privacy governance spanning agent memory, logs, tools, consent, deletion propagation and cross-agent handoffs.
candidates_reviewed.limitations: The taxonomy is an early draft and does not yet provide validated benchmark scores or deployment-specific risk rankings.
candidates_reviewed.rationale: A reviewed primary taxonomy defines an agent-specific runtime privacy mechanism not represented by an existing Watchlist topic.

evidence.title: MLCommons Agent Privacy Risk Taxonomy v0.1

candidates_reviewed.name: Decision models emerge as a separate AI systems layer
candidates_reviewed.mechanism: Typed probabilistic decision models serving routing and control decisions as a distinct systems layer.
candidates_reviewed.mechanism_comparison: Clef is a second Jev-compatible typed decision-model implementation and therefore adds new evidence to the same tracked mechanism.
candidates_reviewed.limitations: Benchmark and latency claims are vendor-reported; independent task-specific calibration and robustness evaluation remain necessary.
candidates_reviewed.rationale: Cloudflare released Clef and Clef-flash as open-source decision models that return probabilities over typed answers, are API-compatible with Jev, support local/open-weight use, and add a second independent implementation of the decision-model systems layer.

candidates_reviewed.name: Agents that overclaim task completion
candidates_reviewed.mechanism: Executable verification of an agent completion claim against terminal backend state and side effects.
candidates_reviewed.mechanism_comparison: ThinkingBox operationalizes the same claim-versus-outcome failure mode with executable terminal-state checks and repeated trials.
candidates_reviewed.limitations: The released benchmark uses synthetic reconstructed enterprise workflows; transfer to every production tool stack and model requires local validation.
candidates_reviewed.rationale: ThinkingBox evaluates stateful agents by executable checks over terminal backend state and side effects, repeats each task 20 times, and documents cases where agents terminate cleanly yet leave the wrong system state, adding concrete evidence for claim-versus-outcome verification.

candidates_reviewed.name: Agent safeguards tailored to the task
candidates_reviewed.mechanism: Capability controls and safeguards calibrated to verified users, tasks and deployment risk.
candidates_reviewed.mechanism_comparison: Anthropic tiered cyber verification adds deployment evidence to the existing task-specific agent-safeguard mechanism.
candidates_reviewed.limitations: The published effectiveness data are first-party and cyber-specific; generalization to non-cyber agent deployments and independent validation remain open.
candidates_reviewed.rationale: Anthropic expanded its Cyber Verification Program into three access tiers that pair stronger cyber capabilities with applicant verification and tier-specific safeguards, providing new deployment evidence for controls tailored to task, user and risk level.
